title: A New Approach to Sales Roleplay
summary: Neha Gupta is the founder and CEO of Breakthrough AI, and she came to sales practice sideways: 25 years at Unilever, Clorox, and mission-driven brands taught her that the people who stall out are rarely the ones who lack technical skill, they are the ones who never learned to sell an idea. Her argument in this episode is that roleplay has always been the right answer and the wrong experience, because a human partner will not push back hard enough and an off-the-shelf LLM is built to agree with you. She walks through what Breakthrough does instead: 11 fine-tuned personas that hold character, a scenario library built on real objections (the buyer who loves everything and still wants 10% off), and a feedback agent that scores micro behaviors like whether you acknowledged the concern and whether you closed with a next step. Listen if you run a sales team, own enablement, or have ever assigned roleplay and quietly watched nobody do it.
keyQuote: What's nice about AI now is that it can be pushy. It doesn't care about your feelings; it can say no.
guestBio: Neha Gupta is the founder and CEO of Breakthrough AI, a practice-first coaching platform where sales teams rehearse high-stakes conversations against AI personas that push back. She started her career in consulting, where she was put in front of skeptical clients early and had to learn corporate communication by watching other people do it. She spent years in consumer brands at Unilever and Clorox, then moved into mission-driven work with leadership roles at SaverLife and her own brand advisory practice, BellyFire Branding. She holds a BA from Stanford and an MBA from the Yale School of Management. As the daughter of immigrants and a first-generation corporate employee, she built Breakthrough around a conviction that executive presence is a learnable skill rather than a birthright.
takeaways: AI roleplay works because the AI does not care about your feelings.
ChatGPT drops a demanding persona after one or two exchanges.
Colleagues are bad roleplay partners; they protect the relationship.
Sales is the only discipline that performs without practicing.
One rubric beats ten managers with ten grading scales.
Pilot users reported 40% less anxiety after practicing.
Run roleplay as a six week competition, not a forever assignment.
Discount talk is a value conversation, not a pricing one.
